frequent_clusters.theme: Authentication, User Roles, RBAC & Login Sessions

canonical_qa.typical_question: How should role-based authentication (Admin vs User) be implemented? Do we need JWT or session cookies?
canonical_qa.best_answer: For MAD-1 (Flask + Jinja2), standard session-based auth (e.g. Flask-Login or session dict) with role checks in decorators is recommended. For MAD-2 (Vue.js + Flask API), JWT token-based authentication (Flask-JWT-Extended) is expected, where tokens are sent in the Authorization header. Ensure admin routes strictly verify user.role == 'admin'.
bullet_points: MAD-1: Session cookies with role checking.
MAD-2: JWT tokens stored in localStorage/sessionStorage.
Always hash passwords with Werkzeug/bcrypt before storing in database.

frequent_clusters.theme: Database Design: SQLite3 vs SQLAlchemy / Raw SQL

canonical_qa.typical_question: Can we use plain sqlite3 or is SQLAlchemy mandatory for the project? What is the difference?
canonical_qa.best_answer: It is completely fine to use SQLite3 directly if it satisfies the required project functionality. Think of it this way: SQLite3 is the actual database where data is stored, while SQLAlchemy is a Python ORM library that allows interacting with the database using Python objects instead of writing raw SQL queries. Using SQLAlchemy makes queries cleaner and relationships easier to maintain.
bullet_points: Both satisfy project requirements as long as functionality works.
SQLAlchemy ORM helps avoid raw SQL injection and syntax errors.
Remember to store the .sqlite3 or .db file in the correct relative path.

frequent_clusters.theme: Async Background Tasks: Celery, Redis & Daily Alerts

canonical_qa.typical_question: How do we trigger daily reminders and monthly reports using Celery & Redis?
canonical_qa.best_answer: Use Celery Beat for scheduled tasks (daily reminders at a specific time) and Celery Worker for asynchronous triggers (e.g., CSV export or monthly PDF generation). Make sure Redis server is running locally on port 6379 before launching the worker.
bullet_points: Start Redis server first: redis-server
Run worker: celery -A app.celery worker -l info
Run periodic scheduler: celery -A app.celery beat -l info
Use MailHog or SMTP for testing email delivery locally.

frequent_clusters.theme: Frontend & Vue.js: API Integration, CORS & Routing

canonical_qa.typical_question: CORS error when calling Flask API from Vue frontend, or router navigation failing?
canonical_qa.best_answer: Install and enable flask_cors: `from flask_cors import CORS; CORS(app)`. In your Vue fetch/axios requests, ensure you pass the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and handle 401 unauthorized redirects in the router navigation guard (`router.beforeEach`).
bullet_points: Enable CORS on Flask: CORS(app, resources={r'/*': {'origins': '*'}})
Verify base API URL in Vue config (e.g., http://localhost:5000/api)
Check DevTools Network tab to inspect Preflight OPTIONS response.
